The randomized, double-blind, multicenter study will compare a new topical Thykamine 0.1% formulation with Glaxal Base cream in adult women undergoing radiotherapy. Its primary measure is time to development of Grade 2 or higher radiodermatitis, or radiation-induced skin inflammation. Treatment will last approximately eight to nine weeks per patient.

The study will evaluate the new formulation against Glaxal Base cream, with the primary objective of assessing the time to development of Grade 2 or higher radiodermatitis. The program builds on Devonian's existing scientific and clinical experience with Thykamine^{™}, while evaluating a formulation specifically developed for radiation-induced skin injury.

Expanding Thykamine^{™} into Supportive Oncology: Addressing an Important Unmet Medical Need

The clinical study will evaluate a new proprietary topical formulation containing Thykamine^{™} 0.1%, specifically developed for the prevention of radiation-induced skin injury.

Unlike the formulation previously evaluated in Devonian's Phase II clinical study in atopic dermatitis, this new formulation has been designed to address the particular challenges associated with skin exposed to ionizing radiation.

Preclinical investigations have demonstrated Thykamine^{™}'s capacity to modulate oxidative stress-related processes. Additional experimental work involving skin models and dermal fibroblasts has explored biological processes associated with tissue repair and extracellular matrix regulation.

These findings support the scientific rationale for evaluating the new formulation in the prevention of radiation-induced skin injury. Its clinical efficacy and safety for this indication remain to be established.

Overview of the Health Canada-Authorized Clinical Study

The 150-patient, randomized, double-blind, multicenter clinical study will evaluate the efficacy and safety of Devonian's new proprietary Thykamine^{™} 0.1% topical formulation compared with Glaxal Base cream in women undergoing radiotherapy for breast cancer.

Key study characteristics:

  * Study population: 150 adult female patients undergoing breast cancer radiotherapy.
  * Study design: Randomized, double-blind, multicenter, parallel-group controlled study.
  * Treatment groups: Thykamine^{™} 0.1% formulation versus Glaxal Base cream (1:1 randomization).
  * Treatment regimen: Topical application three times daily during radiotherapy and for five weeks following treatment.
  * Treatment duration: Approximately eight to nine weeks per patient, depending on the radiotherapy schedule.

Primary efficacy endpoint: Time to development of Grade 2 or higher radiodermatitis, assessed using standardized clinical severity criteria.

Secondary endpoints: Incidence of Grade 2 or higher radiodermatitis, patient-reported pain, patient satisfaction, and adverse events.

The study aims to determine whether Thykamine^{™} 0.1% can prevent or delay the onset of clinically significant radiation-induced skin reactions, potentially improving supportive care for patients undergoing breast cancer radiotherapy.

Exploring a Differentiated Regulatory Pathway to Support Commercialization

An important strategic component of Devonian's radiodermatitis program is the Company's intention to explore a potential medical-device regulatory pathway for its new proprietary Thykamine^{™} formulation, complementing the conventional pharmaceutical development programs being pursued for other indications.

Subject to confirmation of the formulation's regulatory classification, successful clinical development, and satisfaction of applicable regulatory requirements, a medical-device pathway could potentially offer several advantages:

Participants will apply the assigned topical treatment three times daily during radiotherapy and for five weeks afterward. # October 13, 2026: Mounting evidence that popular unapproved peptide causes cancers

## Major Stories

More evidence links melanotan-II to skin cancer. PSM talks to a family advocate about the risks of performance-enhancing drugs and releases our six-month importation update.

Another case report has been published linking the use of melanotan-II to occurrences of skin cancer. Doctors in Michigan and Illinois reported that a man who injected the unregulated peptide developed a melanoma lesion after only taking the drug for five weeks. The man experienced nausea, headaches, appetite loss, and changes in existing moles after obtaining the peptide through his local gym. Although doctors cannot definitively link the melanoma to the drug, the case adds to existing concerns about serious side effects and the risks of using products without established safety standards or medical oversight.

The report echoes concerns raised in a recent KQED podcast about melanotan-II, which has been promoted online despite limited human safety data and potential risks. These conversations come as PSM sat down with the sister of an Australian man who died at 33 after years of using body-enhancing drugs, including peptides. She is sharing his story to raise awareness and prevent other families from experiencing similar loss.

# Biodexa announces another Serenta milestone with 100 patients enrolled in its registrational Phase 3 trial in FAP

PRESS RELEASE GlobeNewswire

Oct. 13, 2026, 08:30 AM

October 13, 2026

Biodexa announces another Serenta milestone
with 100 patients enrolled in its registrational Phase 3 trial in FAP

Update on expected timing of pre-specified futility analysis and database lock

Biodexa Pharmaceuticals PLC (Nasdaq: BDRX) (“Biodexa” or “the Company”), a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company developing innovative products focused on the treatment or prevention of gastrointestinal cancers is pleased to announce that it has enrolled 100 patients in its registrational Phase 3 trial of eRapa in Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP), NCT06950385. The trial, branded “Serenta” is recruiting at 29 clinical sites across the US and five countries in Europe with a further two sites in Canada expected to be initiated shortly.

The Serenta protocol provides for a pre-specified futility analysis after 25 Progression Free Survival (PFS) events and database lock after 75 PFS events in the Serenta trial. The Serenta protocol includes a composite endpoint which defines the nature of the PFS events.

# Global Health & WASH: August 2026 Funding Opportunities (24 new opportunities!)

### 79 funding opportunities - Climate is being written into the definition of health, AI is arriving at the point of care, and epidemic preparedness is being rebuilt around African institutions.

Eliana Summer-Galai

Aug 03, 2026

∙ Paid

1

Share

Hello Everyone,

24 new opportunities on the Global Health and WASH page this cycle, all added since the July mid-month update, and 17 of them closing within the month. Three currents run through them: climate is being absorbed into the definition of health, artificial intelligence is moving from the lab into care delivery, and epidemic preparedness is being rebuilt around African institutions.

Climate is being written into the definition of health. Nexa, co-led by Grand Challenges Canada and the Science for Africa Foundation, states the thesis plainly: climate change is a health delivery crisis, and it funds tools that let communities act on climate-driven risks like mosquito-borne infection and extreme heat. UNICEF is running three separate calls that reframe water and sanitation as climate-resilience work, in Nepal’s Karnali province, in West Java, and across Ecuador’s emergency contingency system. Even the Halton Foundation’s indoor-environmental-quality grants tie building conditions to respiratory health. The climate-health convergence we have tracked all year is no longer a niche; it is becoming the frame through which mainstream health and WASH money is allocated.

AI is being funded at the point of care, not just the bench. The Gates Foundation’s Grand Challenges RFP asks for conversational AI that engages consumers directly on family planning, and its multiplex-diagnostics call wants low-cost tools that read many biomarkers at once. The Francis Crick Institute’s KQ Labs backs startups whose use of data sits at the core of the model, not bolted on, and the Asian Development Bank’s dengue challenge rewards bio-enabled and digitally powered surveillance. The tell is consistent: these funders now treat data and AI capability as a scored expectation of a credible health solution, extending the AI-as-baseline pattern we first named in the spring into frontline delivery.

Epidemic preparedness is being rebuilt around African institutions. Africa CDC’s African Epidemic Services fellowship trains field epidemiologists inside the continent’s own public-health system, the Africa Health Collaborative funds research led by early-career investigators at African member institutions, and the Global Health EDCTP3 prizes recognize teams working across sub-Saharan Africa and Europe.

Biodexa Pharmaceuticals (Nasdaq: BDRX) has enrolled 100 patients in Serenta, its registrational Phase 3 trial of eRapa for familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP). The placebo-controlled trial plans to enroll 168 subjects, randomized 2:1 to drug or placebo. Recruitment is underway at 29 clinical sites across the US and five European countries; two Canadian sites are expected to start shortly.

The protocol calls for a futility analysis after 25 progression-free survival events, assessing whether continuing the trial is warranted, and database lock after 75 events. A composite endpoint defines these events. Based on current event accumulation, Biodexa said the analysis could occur in early 2027 and database lock potentially around year-end 2027, sooner than originally anticipated. The Phase 3 program is supported by a $20 million grant from the Cancer Prevention and Research Institute of Texas.

# Clinical Trials

### Welcome to a resource for information on current research trials in veterinary oncology.

Pet owners often ask us if we are aware of any CLINICAL TRIALS that may be available to their cat or dog who has been diagnosed with cancer. While there certainly are a number of studies occurring around the world, participation in a clinical trial can often be difficult, especially if the trial is going on in a hospital or clinic far away from your home.

Each clinical trial has very specific qualifications for participation that include everything from the breed and age of the participant to the life expectancy, weight and of course the type of cancer. Each study is very particular in its criteria for participation. Something else to take into consideration is that clinical trials are NOT always free. There may be fees to participate because grants may only cover a certain portion of the trial, and you may have to travel a long way to participate for several weeks or months perhaps.

The following links represent an organized effort to provide general practitioners and their pet owners access to information to trials being conducted across the United States and, in some cases, in other countries.

## History

[edit]

Clinique counter at a Farmers department store

In 1967, American Vogue magazine published an article called "Can Great Skin Be Created?",^{[2]} written by beauty editor Carol Phillips with Norman Orentreich, discussing the significance of a skin-care routine. Evelyn Lauder, daughter-in-law of Estée Lauder, read the article and brought it to Estée's attention.^{[3]}^{[4]} Both Carol Phillips and Orentreich were recruited to help create the brand, and in April 1968, Clinique premiered as the world's first allergy tested, dermatologist-driven line at Saks Fifth Avenue in New York, US,^{[5]} launched with 117 products.^{[6]} The brand launched with a 3-step routine for all skin types tailored for all outcomes looking to be achieved by a consumer while bringing a scientific approach to skincare.^{[7]}

The Center has long-established relationships with leaders in the veterinary pharmaceutical industry and maintains collaborative partnerships with other innovative academic centers. In addition to performing clinical trials, the VCIC offers an extensive range of clinical research operations services, including clinical trial project management, recruiting and marketing strategies, trial site selection and monitoring, record auditing, and data quality assurance and control.

## Our Services

The VCIC works closely with corporate sponsors, individual clinicians, clients, and patients, offering services ranging from recruitment, study design, protocol compliance, quality assurance, data capture, and reporting, conducting clinical trials at both Penn Vet hospitals.

### Targeted Marketing & Recruitment Strategies

The VCIC has demonstrated an ability to recruit significant sample sizes in a wide array of disease models over more than 14 years of managing veterinary clinical trials. Ryan Hospital’s large case load combined with its extensive referral network of more than 3,000 veterinary practices make it uniquely suited for clinical trial recruitment and enrollment.
When a trial requires more animals with a specific condition than would normally be presented in the 34,000 pets that come to Ryan Hospital annually, the VCIC has a proven record for targeted recruitment of animals at over 400 percent above baseline presentation rate.
VCIC understands and employs recruitment modalities that are most effective for a given target population and can guide sponsors on the most efficient means to enroll the desired number of animals in a specified period of time for a given study, pain management, and disease specific recommendations.

### Clinical Trial Design and Study Protocol Development

Penn Vet has the expertise to implement and manage all aspects of veterinary clinical trials, from study set-up and recruitment to data collection and analysis, final study reporting and closeout. The center works closely with faculty members trained in epidemiology and trial design to ensure that projects are powered appropriately with a robust plan for statistical analysis in order to yield meaningful results.

### Study Site Selection, Training & Management

The VCIC has the clinical research experience to identify and oversee clinical trial sites that are familiar with the international standards set forth in VICH GL-9 Good Clinical Practice as well as perform training for GCP.

### Study Monitoring

Veterinary research nurses with extensive clinical and monitoring experience work on campus as well as with remote study sites to ensure protocol and regulatory compliance.

DR-Learners for Generalizing CATEs from a Randomized Controlled Trial (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25405)
【turn986academia22】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 2 days ago; 
Title: DR-Learners for Generalizing CATEs from a Randomized Controlled Trial
Authors: Vanessa Rodriguez, Brieuc Lehmann, Karla Diaz-Ordaz
Date: Sun Oct 18 17:03:30 2026

Randomized clinical trials are essential for evaluating interventions, yet average treatment effects can obscure treatment effect heterogeneity, making conditional average treatment effects (CATEs) a natural target. However, restrictive eligibility criteria and differential trial participation can limit the generalizability of these effects to broader target populations. Building on existing DR-Learners, we develop the gDR-Learner for generalizing RCT CATEs to a target population, using cross-fitted machine-learning nuisance estimation. We derive excess-risk bounds in which nuisance errors enter only as products, showing that the estimator achieves oracle-rate convergence despite slower individual nuisance estimation. The variables needed to generalize are rarely measured across the entire target population. We therefore extend the methods to two settings with incomplete covariate information: when certain covariates are measured only in the trial (e.g., biomarkers), and covariates driving trial participation measured only in a subsample of the target population, such as a representative cohort or registry. We construct weighted conformal prediction intervals for individual treatment effects, accounting for covariate shift between the trial and target population. In simulations, the gDR-Learner achieved the lowest estimation error when all covariates were observed relative to standard T- and DR-Learners and an inverse-probability-weighted T-Learner, and also outperformed the latter under incomplete covariate observation. We illustrate the methods by reanalyzing the Coronary Artery Surgery Study, examining treatment effect heterogeneity by prior myocardial infarction and baseline ejection fraction.
